shared_prefix.speaker: Lisa
shared_prefix.message:
Hey John, have you thought about what we should give David for his ordination? I was thinking maybe we could pool some money together as a gift. What do you think? 

Also, I've been hearing some people say it's a duty towards society to have children... I just don't understand that. Do you really believe that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: John
shared_prefix.message:
Pooling money sounds like a practical idea for David's gift. Perhaps something that symbolizes his new journey... like a nice book on spirituality or a beautiful piece of art. 

And yes, I do believe it's a duty towards society to have children. It's about contributing to the future, passing down values, and ensuring that our culture continues. It's important for our communities.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lisa
shared_prefix.message:
I like the idea of a nice book or art for David. Pooling money will definitely help us get something meaningful. 

But about having children... I just can't agree that it's a duty. People can contribute to society in many ways, not just through having kids. There are so many different paths in life that can create positive change. Don't you see that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: John
shared_prefix.message: I appreciate your perspective on contributing to society in different ways. But when you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us — wanting to make a difference. Deep down, we are all the same. Having children is just one way to ensure our values and culture continue. Of course, there are many paths to positive change, but I believe a family also brings a unique joy and fulfillment that contributes to our communities. It's a small world after all, and we're all in this together, right?
